meta.scope: examples/larder: server API, web app, schema, tests, tooling and docs
meta.method: Static subtraction review against the purpose baseline, entry points and consumers in units.json

summary: Larder exists to track one household's pantry and send an email reminder; much of the repository does not serve that. Five elements are active liabilities: a finished A/B test still writes visitor IPs on every request, /debug/dump hands out every secret, a Stripe webhook accepts unsigned writes after Stripe was removed, a Mailchimp key is kept for a dead integration, and sign-in asks for full calendar access. Beyond what is unused, two features are used but do not earn their place: a household leaderboard serving a documented non-goal, and a four-channel notification registry for an email-only job. Subtracting them leaves the same product, smaller and easier to change.

findings.title: A finished A/B test still runs on every request and stores visitor IPs

findings.basis: The module says the experiment ended 2025-03-31 and variant A won (server/ab_test.py:1; inventory markers, overdue). Nothing reads experiment_assignments or the bucket: no SELECT, no cookie read besides the guard.
findings.impact: A database write on every request without a bucket cookie, and personal data (IP addresses) collected for a purpose that no longer exists.

subtraction.what: server/ab_test.py and the before_request hook at server/app.py:14.
subtraction.remains: Requests go straight to their handlers; variant A pricing is already the only pricing.
subtraction.loses: Nothing: no caller, user or job depends on it.

findings.risk: None in code. The table it fills is P-009; drop it only after its retention question is settled.

validation.evidence: grep experiment_assignments: only the INSERT at server/ab_test.py:9 and the DDL; grep bucket: no reader.
validation.dynamic_checked: Searched getattr/registry dispatch, templates, CI and docs for assign_bucket and the table name; none.

findings.basis: No code imports stripe (inventory unimported_dependencies), no screen takes payment, and nothing reads payments.
findings.impact: Anyone can write rows into payments; the endpoint exists only as attack surface.

subtraction.remains: No payment surface at all, which matches the product.
subtraction.loses: Nothing in the app; Stripe may log failed deliveries until its endpoint is deleted.

findings.risk: Stripe may still be configured to deliver events here; confirm in the Stripe dashboard (decisions).

validation.evidence: grep stripe: the route, payments.stripe_id and the pin; no import, no SELECT on payments.
validation.dynamic_checked: The only possible caller is outside the repository (Stripe); not observable statically.
